item.title: [NVDA Bullish (+0.28)] Equinix director Paisley sells $4.08m in stock
item.description:
Sentiment: NVDA Bullish (+0.28)
Christopher B. Paisley, a director at Equinix Inc. (NASDAQ:EQIX), disposed of 4,000 shares of common stock valued at $4,077,120. This transaction involved contributing shares to an exchange fund, with the stock valued at $1,019.28 per share, aligning closely with its current trading price. The company has seen a 35% gain year-to-date, though InvestingPro analysis suggests it is overvalued.

item.title: [MSFT Neutral (+0.11), NVDA Bullish (+0.47)] Hugging Face approached Nvidia’s Huang weeks ahead of $12.9B acquisition, CEO tells CNBC
item.description:
Sentiment: MSFT Neutral (+0.11), NVDA Bullish (+0.47)
Nvidia has agreed to acquire open-source AI platform Hugging Face for $12.9 billion, marking its second-largest acquisition. Hugging Face CEO Clément Delangue initiated contact with Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang over the summer, seeking more resources and scale for the company amidst a turning point for open-source AI. This acquisition signifies Nvidia's continued expansion beyond hardware and into the broader AI ecosystem, emphasizing the importance of open models despite recent security concerns.

item.title: [NVDA Bullish (+0.33)] SLB’s Kelvion Deal Could Change How Investors Value the Oilfield Giant
item.description:
Sentiment: NVDA Bullish (+0.33)
SLB's acquisition of Kelvion for $4.1 billion signals a strategic pivot towards data center solutions, aiming for $4.5 billion to $5 billion in revenue for its Data Center Solutions business by 2028. This move provides SLB with crucial thermal-management capabilities for data centers, complementing its existing NVIDIA partnership and potentially diversifying its growth story away from its declining oilfield earnings. The deal is expected to be accretive without share dilution, and while the data center segment is not yet transformative, it positions SLB for a revaluation as two distinct businesses.

item.title: [MSFT Bullish (+0.40)] Euromonitor agrees integration with Microsoft 365 Copilot
item.description:
Sentiment: MSFT Bullish (+0.40)
Euromonitor International has integrated its Passport platform with Microsoft 365 Copilot, allowing users to access market insights and intelligence through a new agent. This integration enables natural language queries within Copilot, supported by Anthropic's model context protocol (MCP). The aim is to provide clients with a faster, secure way to incorporate Euromonitor's data into their daily workflows and decision-making processes.

item.title: [MSFT Bullish (+0.16)] Palo Alto Networks earnings highlight SASE and network security wins
item.description:
Sentiment: MSFT Bullish (+0.16)
Palo Alto Networks reported strong Q4 FY26 earnings with $3.41 billion in revenue, a 34% YoY increase, driven by SASE and network security platform adoption. The company also announced its fifth acquisition of the year, Console, an agentic AI security platform, to enhance its Cortex platform. CEO Nikesh Arora highlighted the growing urgency among customers to fortify defenses against AI-redefined security threats and the company's focus on operational technology vulnerabilities.

item.title: [NVDA Bullish (+0.26)] Raymond James raises Snowflake stock price target on AI growth
item.description:
Sentiment: NVDA Bullish (+0.26)
Raymond James has increased its price target for Snowflake Inc. (NYSE:SNOW) to $425 from $275, maintaining an Outperform rating, following strong Q2 fiscal 2027 results. The company's product revenue growth accelerated for the third consecutive quarter, largely driven by AI products like Cortex Copilot and CoWork. While the stock may appear overvalued at present, analysts anticipate profitability this year, and other firms like Citizens and Deutsche Bank have also raised their price targets for Snowflake, underscoring growing demand for its data platform and AI offerings.

item.title: [AMZN Bullish (+0.25)] Amazon.com, Inc. $AMZN Shares Acquired by Symmetry Partners LLC

Symmetry Partners LLC increased its stake in Amazon.com, Inc. by 14.7% in the second quarter, bringing its total holdings to 19,788 shares valued at $4.7 million. Institutional investors now own 72.2% of AMZN, while the company reported strong Q2 earnings of $5.75 per share against a $1.82 consensus, with revenue up 19.6% year-over-year. Despite positive analyst sentiment and a "Moderate Buy" rating, risks include insider selling and an FTC lawsuit regarding advertising practices.

item.title: [AAPL Bullish (+0.27)] A Rare Working "Hatfield" Apple-1 Could Fetch Up to $800,000 USD at Bonhams
item.description:
Sentiment: AAPL Bullish (+0.27)
Bonhams will auction the "Hatfield" Apple-1, a rare and still-functional example of Apple's first pre-assembled personal computer, with an estimated value of $500,000 to $800,000 USD. The unit, traceable to its original owner, includes a motherboard signed by Steve Wozniak and a 1978 letter signed by Steve Jobs. It is ranked No. 48 on the Apple-1 Registry as one of only 74 verified survivors, with even fewer remaining operational.

item.title: [NVDA Neutral (+0.08)] Billionaire Dan Loeb Exited Nvidia and Broadcom. Is He Calling the Top in AI Chips?
item.description:
Sentiment: NVDA Neutral (+0.08)
Billionaire investor Dan Loeb's Third Point hedge fund sold its remaining Nvidia and Broadcom shares in Q2, sparking speculation about his outlook on AI chips. However, the filing does not explicitly state Loeb called a sector top, and the positions were a small part of his firm's total portfolio. The article suggests the exits could be due to portfolio construction, valuation, or opportunity cost rather than a unified negative view on the AI chip industry.

item.title: [NVDA Bullish (+0.23)] Broadcom stock wavers as chipmaker's strong results 'not enough to keep investors happy'
item.description:
Sentiment: NVDA Bullish (+0.23)
Broadcom's stock wavered despite reporting strong fiscal Q3 results, including significant revenue growth and an earnings beat, driven by high demand for AI chips. Analysts noted that while the results were strong, they weren't enough to satisfy investors' high expectations, especially given the company's leverage to AI. The chipmaker exceeded revenue and EPS expectations but provided a slightly lower-than-consensus revenue forecast for the current quarter.

item.title: [NVDA Bullish (+0.45)] Capsule Security fine-tunes Nvidia Nemotron models to stop rogue AI agents
item.description:
Sentiment: NVDA Bullish (+0.45)
Capsule Security has launched a new detection system, dubbed an "AI circuit breaker," built on fine-tuned Nvidia Nemotron models to prevent rogue AI agents from executing unintended actions. This system operates as a real-time control layer, allowing customers to approve, flag, or block agent actions before damage occurs. It boasts 98% accuracy on academic benchmarks and aims to secure autonomous agents that have access to sensitive data and infrastructure.

item.title: [NVDA Bullish (+0.30)] Super Micro Computer (SMCI) Joins A Major Enterprise AI Infrastructure Build
item.description:
Sentiment: NVDA Bullish (+0.30)
Super Micro Computer (SMCI) has announced a partnership with Cisco to provide high-density liquid and air-cooled compute systems for AI infrastructure, integrating its systems into Cisco's Secure AI Factory architecture which leverages NVIDIA technologies. This collaboration expands Super Micro Computer's access to enterprise, neocloud, and sovereign cloud customers, reinforcing its position in the AI server market. The deal is seen as supporting Super Micro's strategy for repeatable, large-scale AI data center projects and potentially driving recurring, high-value orders globally, though analysts note potential margin pressure due to Cisco's influence over system design and pricing.

item.title: [MSFT Bullish (+0.42)] NCSA and Microsoft Join Forces to Drive Zero Trust Strategy, Advancing Cybersecurity Readiness for Thai Organizations in AI Era
item.description:
Sentiment: MSFT Bullish (+0.42)
The National Cyber Security Agency (NCSA) and Microsoft co-organized a workshop to promote Zero Trust security principles and AI capabilities among Thai organizations. This initiative aims to strengthen cybersecurity readiness across public, private, and critical infrastructure sectors in Thailand, given the increasing complexity of cyber threats and the rapid adoption of AI by threat actors. The workshop provided guidance on implementing Zero Trust strategies, aligning with national cybersecurity laws and global standards, and developing tailored roadmaps for organizations.

item.title: [NVDA Bullish (+0.31)] Soros Fund Management Increased Micron Nearly Eightfold. Is AI Memory Still One of the Best Chip Trades?
item.description:
Sentiment: NVDA Bullish (+0.31)
Soros Fund Management significantly increased its stake in Micron Technology (MU) during Q2, raising its share count by nearly 700% to 22,422 shares valued at $25.9 million. This move highlights memory's critical role in AI infrastructure, as high-bandwidth memory (HBM) is essential for AI accelerators. While the purchase indicates growing institutional interest in Micron, the article cautions that the AI memory trade is no longer overlooked and its future success depends on supply discipline and sustained HBM demand.

item.title: [AAPL Neutral (+0.13), NVDA Neutral (+0.14)] Broadcom beats expectations as AI labs double down on custom chips
item.description:
Sentiment: AAPL Neutral (+0.13), NVDA Neutral (+0.14)
Broadcom Inc. exceeded earnings and revenue expectations in its third-quarter financial report, primarily driven by its semiconductor business and increasing demand from AI labs for custom chips. Despite strong performance and optimistic long-term projections for its AI revenue, the company's stock declined due to a conservative forecast for the current quarter which fell short of Wall Street estimates. Broadcom is actively collaborating with major AI players like Google, OpenAI, and Meta, developing specialized processors to support their growing AI infrastructure needs.

item.title: [NVDA Bullish (+0.33)] Broadcom and Cisco make AI factory deployment workload-driven
item.description:
Sentiment: NVDA Bullish (+0.33)
Broadcom and Cisco Systems are partnering to simplify AI factory deployment by making it a workload-sizing exercise rather than a complex custom infrastructure project. Their solution combines VMware Cloud Foundation and Cisco Unified Computing System infrastructure, mapping specific AI workloads to appropriate hardware. This approach aims to transform IT departments from AI infrastructure builders into AI consumers, enabling faster, fully configured AI factory deployments.

item.title: [MSFT Bullish (+0.46)] Microsoft Discloses Exact Azure Sales Figures For The First Time Following Longstanding Investor Demand
item.description:
Sentiment: MSFT Bullish (+0.46)
Microsoft has announced it will begin providing specific quarterly revenue metrics for its Azure cloud platform, a move long awaited by investors. The company also revealed historical Azure sales, which reached $29.4 billion in the quarter ending June 2026 and over $100 billion for the most recent fiscal year. This increased transparency and a strategic reorganization of its core divisions reflect the growing impact of AI on Microsoft's business model.

item.title: [AMZN Neutral (+0.13)] How Equinix has found a niche in the multitrillion-dollar AI data center boom
item.description:
Sentiment: AMZN Neutral (+0.13)
Equinix, a legacy data center company, has strategically positioned itself to benefit from the AI boom by partnering with Nvidia and Together AI, allowing customers flexible ways to run AI models. Despite being a colocation facility rather than a hyperscaler, Equinix's stock is up 33% this year, raising its market cap to $100 billion. The company's focus on inference and urban data center locations gives it a unique advantage in the evolving AI landscape, even as some investors remain skeptical about its growth potential.

item.title: [MSFT Bullish (+0.30)] Microsoft updates segment reporting structure for fiscal 2027
item.description:
Sentiment: MSFT Bullish (+0.30)
Microsoft announced a new segment reporting structure for fiscal year 2027, reorganizing its business into "Agents and Infra" and "Devices and Consumer" segments. The company maintained its overall first-quarter revenue guidance while providing specific outlooks for each new segment. Azure revenue growth is projected to be 44% to 45% in constant currency for the first quarter.

item.title: [MSFT Bullish (+0.31), AMZN Bullish (+0.23)] Microsoft to start disclosing Azure quarterly revenue as company consolidates business units
item.description:
Sentiment: MSFT Bullish (+0.31), AMZN Bullish (+0.23)
Microsoft announced it will begin disclosing quarterly revenue for its Azure cloud business, providing more transparency about its competition with Amazon Web Services and Google. This change is part of a broader restructuring that consolidates the company's internal operating segments from three to two. CEO Satya Nadella stated that this new reporting structure will define Azure more purely as their consumption-based platform and infrastructure business, emphasizing the impact of AI on the company's products and business models.

item.title: [AMZN Bearish (-0.21)] DOJ expands beef antitrust inquiry to Amazon, Walmart, others
item.description:
Sentiment: AMZN Bearish (-0.21)
The U.S. Justice Department has broadened its antitrust investigation into the meatpacking industry by requesting six years of beef pricing and procurement data from eight major retailers, including Amazon, Costco, and Walmart. This inquiry stems from record-high beef prices contributing significantly to food inflation, prompting President Donald Trump to publicly request a probe last year. The department is seeking detailed information on purchasing strategies, retail pricing, profit margins, and market analysis from these grocers to understand the drivers behind the escalating costs.

item.title: [AMZN Neutral (+0.11)] South Korea's semiconductor exports just tripled year-over-year. Is it too much of a good thing?
item.description:
Sentiment: AMZN Neutral (+0.11)
South Korea's semiconductor exports surged 209% year-over-year in August to a record $46.65 billion, accounting for nearly half of the country's total goods exports. This boom is largely driven by AI infrastructure demand. While positive for the economy, economists are concerned about the potential impact if this rapid growth slows down abruptly, especially given challenges in other traditional sectors and ongoing monetary policy tightening.

item.title: [AAPL Neutral (+0.13), MSFT Bullish (+0.45), AMZN Neutral (+0.13)] Is Microsoft Stock Winning The Move To The Cloud Or Just The AI Boom?
item.category: AAPL Neutral (+0.13), MSFT Bullish (+0.45), AMZN Neutral (+0.13)
item.description:
Sentiment: AAPL Neutral (+0.13), MSFT Bullish (+0.45), AMZN Neutral (+0.13)
Microsoft's growth engine has shifted from cloud migrations to AI consumption, with the company focusing on monetizing AI workloads and Azure AI platform adoption. While Azure's 43% growth is driven by AI, the overall Intelligent Cloud segment still grows at 32%. This change indicates Microsoft's successful pivot to a recurring, consumption-based AI model, and its future performance hinges significantly on continued AI adoption.

item.title: [AAPL Bullish (+0.32)] Apple's Foldable iPhone May Contribute $14 Billion to December Quarter Revenue, Morgan Stanley Says
item.description:
Sentiment: AAPL Bullish (+0.32)
Morgan Stanley projects that Apple's upcoming foldable iPhone could add approximately $14 billion to the company's December quarter revenue. This forecast highlights the potential financial impact of Apple's entry into the foldable smartphone market. The article is from MT Newswires, suggesting a focus on financial analysis and market predictions.

item.title: [AAPL Bullish (+0.27)] MapQuest surges to No. 1 in App Store after Google, Apple adopt Trump’s ‘Lake America’
item.description:
Sentiment: AAPL Bullish (+0.27)
MapQuest has reached the top spot in Apple's App Store after refusing to adopt President Trump's controversial renaming of Lake Ontario to "Lake America." This surge in popularity comes as Google and Apple have both implemented the name change on their respective map apps following a presidential executive order. MapQuest stated its decision was based on preserving names familiar to its users, leading to widespread support and app downloads.

item.title: [AAPL Neutral (+0.12)] Rare, Working Apple I Computer Heads To Auction
item.description:
Sentiment: AAPL Neutral (+0.12)
A rare, working Apple I computer, known as the "Hatfield" Apple I, is heading to auction again with an expected sale price of $500,000 to $800,000. This particular machine, signed by Steve Wozniak, is one of fewer than 75 surviving Apple I computers and includes a letter signed by Steve Jobs offering a trade-in. The computer will be toured by Bonhams before its October 14 auction.

item.title: [AAPL Bullish (+0.35)] Comparing Global ETFs: Vanguard's VXUS vs. State Street's Climate-Focused NZAC
item.description:
Sentiment: AAPL Bullish (+0.35)
This article compares two global ETFs: Vanguard's VXUS and State Street's climate-focused NZAC. VXUS offers broad exposure to non-U.S. markets with a low expense ratio, while NZAC invests in companies aligned with net-zero climate goals, including U.S. stocks. The choice between them depends on an investor's goals, with VXUS providing broader international diversification and NZAC focusing on climate-conscious investments.

item.title: [AAPL Neutral (+0.11)] Jim Cramer has a strong message for Nvidia stock investors
item.description:
Sentiment: AAPL Neutral (+0.11)
Jim Cramer is urging Nvidia to implement a massive $500 billion share buyback, arguing that the company's stock is not being adequately rewarded for its growth. He points to Apple's successful history of large buybacks as a model. Cramer believes such a move would signal management's confidence, reduce share count, and provide consistent demand for the stock.

item.title: [AAPL Bullish (+0.41)] Apple to Mac developers: It’s time to let go of Intel
item.description:
Sentiment: AAPL Bullish (+0.41)
Apple has informed developers that they can now discontinue support for Intel-based Macs for universal macOS apps requiring macOS 13 or later. This move follows Apple's introduction of M-series chips nearly six years ago and its announcement that macOS 26 Tahoe would be the last version to support Intel Macs. Developers will need to assess their user base to determine when to fully transition away from Intel code, especially since macOS 27 will no longer run Intel-only apps on Apple silicon.

item.title: [AAPL Neutral (+0.14)] A look inside Apple’s relationships with Intel and TSMC
item.description:
Sentiment: AAPL Neutral (+0.14)
This article examines Apple's complex relationships with chip manufacturers Intel and TSMC, highlighting how a lack of trust led Apple to move away from Intel and embrace TSMC. It discusses Intel's struggles to regain Apple's business due to issues like a perceived lack of commitment to manufacturing capacity and prematurely discussing potential deals. In contrast, TSMC's strong emphasis on trust, continuous investment in advanced technology, and discretion have solidified its position as Apple's preferred supplier.

item.title: [MSFT Neutral (-0.15)] How Will NetApp Stock React To Its Upcoming Earnings?
item.description:
Sentiment: MSFT Neutral (-0.15)
NetApp (NASDAQ:NTAP) is scheduled to report its earnings on September 2, 2026. This article analyzes the historical stock performance following earnings announcements to predict how NTAP might react. Based on past data, NetApp has shown positive one-day returns post-earnings about 53% of the time over the last five years, with notable correlations between short-term and medium-term returns for strategic trading.

item.title: [MSFT Neutral (+0.03)] A Microsoft Bull Just Closed $36 Million in Call Spreads That Do Not Expire Until 2027
item.description:
Sentiment: MSFT Neutral (+0.03)
A Microsoft options trader recently unwound $36 million in long-dated bullish call spreads set to expire in December 2027, raising questions about future stock performance. Despite strong Azure growth and significant commercial backlogs, Microsoft's increased capital expenditures for FY2027 have impacted free cash flow, contributing to the stock's flat performance over the past year. The article debates whether this early exit signals doubt or simply a profit-taking decision in light of the company's substantial investments in AI infrastructure.

item.title: [MSFT Neutral (+0.01)] Microsoft will stop finishing your sentences in Word and Outlook
item.description:
Sentiment: MSFT Neutral (+0.01)
Microsoft is changing the default setting for text predictions in Word and Outlook, turning them off by default. While the feature will remain available for users who prefer it, Microsoft acknowledges that the suggestions can be an interruption for some. This change applies to Word for Windows, web, iOS, and Android, as well as classic Outlook for Windows and Outlook for Mac, allowing users more flexibility to customize their writing experience.

item.title: [MSFT Bullish (+0.34)] Workday Named Leader in Gartner Magic Quadrant for Eleventh Year
item.description:
Sentiment: MSFT Bullish (+0.34)
Workday has been recognized as a Leader in the Gartner Magic Quadrant for Cloud HCM Suites for the eleventh consecutive year, reflecting its continuous innovation in HR, finance, and IT, and integration of AI to enhance efficiency and employee experience. The company is trusted by over 11,500 organizations, including more than 65% of the Fortune 500, validating its reliability and market position. Recent Q2 FY2027 results show strong AI-driven growth and an optimistic financial outlook for FY2027.

item.title: [AAPL Neutral (+0.14)] Apple’s New CEO Pay Package Is Worth $58 Million, Putting Him Just Outside the Top 20
item.description:
Sentiment: AAPL Neutral (+0.14)
John Ternus, Apple's new CEO, is set to receive a compensation package worth $58 million in his first full year, including a $3 million annual salary and $55 million in equity. This package places him outside the top 20 highest-paid S&P 500 CEOs, specifically at 22nd, behind his predecessor Tim Cook, who had a $74 million package in 2025. The article highlights a general trend of increasing executive compensation, with more CEOs earning over $100 million recently.

item.title: [AMZN Bullish (+0.21)] Can Hedging and Long-Term PPAs Strengthen Vistra's Growth?
item.description:
Sentiment: AMZN Bullish (+0.21)
Vistra Corp. is enhancing its earnings visibility and stability through a dual strategy of disciplined hedging and long-term Power Purchase Agreements (PPAs). This approach, which includes significant contracts with Amazon Web Services and Meta, aims to reduce exposure to volatile wholesale power prices and convert more merchant generation into contracted revenues, ensuring more balanced earnings and supporting long-term investments. While Vistra's shares have declined recently, the stock trades at a discount compared to its industry, and its strategy is similar to other utilities like NRG Energy and NextEra Energy.

item.title: [MSFT Bullish (+0.47), AMZN Bullish (+0.31)] Microsoft's AI Datacenter Expansion: A Game Changer for the Stock?
item.description:
Sentiment: MSFT Bullish (+0.47), AMZN Bullish (+0.31)
Microsoft is expanding its AI datacenter footprint, with a new Saudi Arabia East datacenter region becoming available in November 2026, contributing to an estimated $44 billion in economic activity. This expansion is part of a broader strategy, reflected in its Q4 fiscal 2026 results which showed significant revenue growth in Azure and cloud services. While Microsoft's capital expenditures are substantial, analysts note the stock's valuation appears high compared to the industry.

item.title: [MSFT Bullish (+0.19)] Gartner Warns CX AI Budgets Are Surging
item.description:
Sentiment: MSFT Bullish (+0.19)
Gartner's latest research reveals that customer service leaders' AI spending has jumped 38%, while overall service budgets only increased by two percent. This significant reallocation of funds indicates AI is becoming a core operating cost, forcing CX leaders to prioritize governance, demonstrate ROI, and build trust in AI solutions. The study also highlights the growing importance of AI agents and the need for robust oversight to ensure measurable business value and avoid operational and compliance risks.

item.title: [MSFT Bullish (+0.23)] Using AI for revenue growth is elusive but possible, experts say
item.description:
Sentiment: MSFT Bullish (+0.23)
Experts suggest that while using AI for revenue growth is challenging, it is achievable. TD Bank Group aims to achieve $1 billion in annual value from AI, split between revenue uplift and cost savings, and has already reported significant progress. Other companies are also shifting their AI focus from solely productivity gains to more transformative revenue-generating projects, despite many still struggling to see clear financial returns from their AI investments.

item.title: [AMZN Neutral (+0.12)] The Buzziest New Show on Netflix? A Video Game Trailer
item.description:
Sentiment: AMZN Neutral (+0.12)
Netflix recently experienced a massive, worldwide viewership event that caused tech issues and topped its charts, not with a movie or TV show, but with an exclusive "extended look" trailer for the highly anticipated video game, Grand Theft Auto VI. This phenomenon highlights a growing trend among streaming platforms like Disney and Amazon Prime Video to diversify content beyond traditional film and television, incorporating elements like TikToks, mobile-first video, and video games to drive engagement and cater to evolving consumer preferences. The article suggests that as entertainment lines blur, streaming services are increasingly exploring ancillary opportunities to capture consumer attention.

item.title: [AMZN Neutral (+0.14)] NetApp earnings today: AI momentum meets high expectations By Investing.com
item.description:
Sentiment: AMZN Neutral (+0.14)
NetApp Inc. is reporting its first-quarter fiscal 2027 results today, with analysts expecting significant year-over-year growth in EPS and revenue, though sequentially lower than the previous quarter. Investors are keenly watching whether the company can convert its numerous AI design wins into sustained revenue and grow its Public Cloud segment. The company faces high expectations following a strong prior quarter, with options data suggesting another volatile stock reaction.

item.title: [AMZN Neutral (+0.12)] Adobe acquires Indian market intelligence startup Rilo
item.description:
Sentiment: AMZN Neutral (+0.12)
Adobe has acquired Rilo, an India-based marketing intelligence startup, in a deal that includes licensing and the acquisition of its six-member team. Rilo's technology, which focuses on automating marketing workflows, is expected to enhance Adobe's existing products, particularly for larger customers. This marks Adobe's second acquisition from India, following Rephrase.ai in 2023, as the company continues to bolster its AI-powered marketing capabilities.

item.title: [AAPL Neutral (+0.13)] Wolfe Research Begins Coverage on Hilton Worldwide (NYSE:HLT)
item.description:
Sentiment: AAPL Neutral (+0.13)
Wolfe Research initiated coverage on Hilton Worldwide (NYSE:HLT) with a "peer perform" rating, while the broader analyst consensus remains a "Moderate Buy" with a target price of $353.82. Hilton recently reported strong quarterly EPS of $2.29, surpassing expectations, and revenue growth of 6.5% year-over-year. The company provided optimistic guidance for both the third quarter and full-year 2026 EPS.

item.title: [TSM Neutral (+0.02)] Licensable picture: Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Co Ltd Chairman Morris Chang answers a question in Taipei
item.description:

This Reuters licensable picture shows Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Co Ltd (TSMC) Chairman Morris Chang speaking at an investor conference in Taipei on July 16, 2014. item.title: [AMZN Neutral (+0.14)] 11 Forgotten Books Every ’90s Kid Loved Growing Up
item.description:
Sentiment: AMZN Neutral (+0.14)
This article looks back at 11 popular children's book series from the 1990s that, despite their initial success and presence at Scholastic book fairs, are now largely out of print or forgotten. It covers titles like Animorphs, Give Yourself Goosebumps, Sweet Valley Twins, and Dear America, highlighting their unique premises, publication history, and eventual decline in popularity. The author emphasizes how these books were once integral to the reading experience of '90s kids.

item.title: [AMZN Neutral (+0.10)] ChronoScale and Microsoft partner on 50MW deployment in North America
item.description:
Sentiment: AMZN Neutral (+0.10)
Microsoft is collaborating with ChronoScale, Applied Digital's cloud spin-off, on a 50MW AI infrastructure deployment in the US. This deployment will utilize Nvidia GB300 NVL72 systems and liquid cooling, designed to support high-density accelerated computing. ChronoScale, which recently spun out from Applied Digital, aims to provide production-ready AI compute with high performance and scalability.

item.title: [AMZN Bullish (+0.48)] Cathie Wood’s ARK Invest Says Amazon Has a Potential $1 Trillion AI Business Hiding in Plain Sight
item.description:
Sentiment: AMZN Bullish (+0.48)
ARK Invest projects that Amazon Web Services (AWS) could become a "trillion-dollar-per-year" revenue business due to accelerating AI demand. The firm also highlights that Amazon’s AI-enhanced shopping features, particularly through Alexa, are leading U.S. consumers to spend 40% more per order. This bullish outlook is driven by surging infrastructure investments and the growth of "Agentic Commerce" in retail.

item.title: [AMZN Neutral (+0.14)] Uber lays off 3,300 employees as it restructures for faster growth
item.description:
Sentiment: AMZN Neutral (+0.14)
Uber is laying off approximately 3,300 employees, about 10% of its global workforce, as part of a restructuring effort to reduce management layers and simplify operations. The company aims to reallocate resources to its core ride-hailing, delivery, and robotaxi businesses, while also tightening remote-work policies to concentrate teams in global hubs. CEO Dara Khosrowshahi stated that the savings from these changes will be reinvested in growth, innovation, and autonomous technology.

item.title: [AMZN Bullish (+0.31)] Equinix Unveils Equinix Fabric One, Redefining How Enterprises Connect Across AI, Cloud and Networking Infrastructure
item.description:
Sentiment: AMZN Bullish (+0.31)
Equinix has announced Equinix Fabric One, a new managed connectivity service aimed at simplifying how enterprises connect their distributed cloud, network, and AI environments. This service, leveraging open connectivity specifications from AWS and Google Cloud, will automatically orchestrate and manage connectivity. Equinix Fabric One is designed to reduce the complexity of enterprise networking in the AI era and is expected to enter beta later this year, with general availability in 2027.

item.title: [AAPL Bullish (+0.45)] Tim Cook Steps Down After Fueling a 2,200 Percent Rally for Apple
item.description:
Sentiment: AAPL Bullish (+0.45)
Tim Cook is stepping down as CEO of Apple after overseeing a period of significant growth where the company's stock rallied by 2,200 percent. Under Cook's leadership, Apple's revenue compounded at 7.8 percent annually, and strategic share buybacks reduced the share count by over 40 percent, leading to a substantial increase in the stock's valuation multiple. His successor, John Ternus, will now face the challenge of finding new avenues for business expansion.

item.title: [AAPL Bullish (+0.30)] Apple, SLB And A Financial Stock: CNBC’s ‘Final Trades’
item.description:
Sentiment: AAPL Bullish (+0.30)
On CNBC’s "Halftime Report Final Trades," experts recommended Apple (AAPL), The Goldman Sachs Group (GS), and SLB N.V. (SLB). Joshua Brown picked Apple following John Ternus's succession as CEO, with Rosenblatt maintaining a Neutral rating and raising its price target. Jason Snipe chose Goldman Sachs, which was upgraded by HSBC, while Stephanie Link recommended SLB due to its acquisition of Kelvion to strengthen its Data Center Solutions business.

item.title: [AAPL Bullish (+0.24), AMZN Bullish (+0.20)] Should Tesla Be Kicked Out Of Magnificent 7?
item.description:
Sentiment: AAPL Bullish (+0.24), AMZN Bullish (+0.20)
The article argues that Tesla should be removed from the "Magnificent 7" group of tech stocks because it is primarily an automaker, not a tech company, and its performance has lagged significantly behind its peers. While other Magnificent 7 companies are heavily investing in AI infrastructure, Tesla's core business remains car manufacturing, with its AI ventures like Full Self-Driving and Optimus robots still in early stages and facing skepticism. The author suggests the group should be called the "Mag6" to reflect the true tech focus of the remaining companies.

item.title: [AMZN Bullish (+0.21)] Billionaire Philippe Laffont Increased Micron 19-Fold and Added 49% to Amazon. Is This One Giant AI Demand Bet?
item.description:
Sentiment: AMZN Bullish (+0.21)
Billionaire Philippe Laffont's Coatue Management significantly increased its positions in Micron Technology (MU) and Amazon.com (AMZN) in the second quarter. This move suggests a major bet on the AI demand cycle, with Micron providing high-bandwidth memory for AI systems and Amazon offering cloud services through AWS. The strategy aims to capitalize on both the component scarcity and the infrastructure ownership within the AI supply chain.

item.title: [AAPL Neutral (+0.08)] Jim Cramer: Hyperscalers 'Wrecked Their Balance Sheets', But Apple Carries Twice Alphabet's Debt
item.description:
Sentiment: AAPL Neutral (+0.08)
Jim Cramer praised Apple's "pristine" balance sheet while criticizing hyperscalers for excessive AI data center spending, but financial filings reveal Apple carries significantly more debt than Alphabet. Despite Apple's higher debt load and negative retained earnings due to extensive stock buybacks, the market rewards it with a higher P/E ratio due to its substantial liquidity. The article questions whether Apple's balance sheet will remain pristine if it significantly increases AI infrastructure spending under its new leadership.

item.title: [AAPL Bullish (+0.45)] Apple’s loaded month kicks off with ‘huge launch’ next week
item.description:
Sentiment: AAPL Bullish (+0.45)
September is set to be a monumental month for Apple, featuring the first major event under new CEO John Ternus on September 9th. The company is expected to unveil its first folding iPhone (iPhone Ultra), evolutionary iPhone 18 Pro/Max models, and new Apple Watch Series 12 and Ultra 4 devices. Additionally, significant software updates like iOS 27 with an all-new Siri AI will be released, alongside new Apple TV+ content and Apple Arcade games.

item.title: [AAPL Bullish (+0.34)] Gene Munster Says Apple Has the ‘Upper Hand’ in OpenAI Lawsuit - Apple (NASDAQ:AAPL)
item.description:
Sentiment: AAPL Bullish (+0.34)
Gene Munster of Deepwater Asset Management believes Apple has the "upper hand" in its trade secrets lawsuit against OpenAI, citing newly presented evidence. Apple alleges a former employee, now at OpenAI, downloaded confidential schematics and retained unauthorized access to Apple data. OpenAI, however, denies the allegations, blaming Apple's offboarding process for any continued access and calling the dispute "a mess of Apple’s own making."

item.title: [AAPL Neutral (+0.11)] Apple sets pay targets at $58 Million for new CEO John Ternus, $47 million for Tim Cook
item.description:
Sentiment: AAPL Neutral (+0.11)
Apple has announced compensation packages for its new CEO John Ternus and executive chairman Tim Cook. Ternus is set to receive a package worth $58 million for fiscal year 2027, including a $3 million base salary and $55 million in stock. Cook, transitioning to executive chairman, will have a compensation package of $47 million, with his salary reduced to $2 million.

item.title: [TSM Bullish (+0.86)] TSMC will invest an additional $100 billion into Arizona operations
item.description:
Sentiment: TSM Bullish (+0.86)
Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company (TSMC) announced an additional $100 billion investment in its Arizona operations, bringing its total U.S. commitment to $265 billion. This expansion will fund four more semiconductor fabrication plants and advanced packaging facilities, solidifying Arizona's role as a key hub for advanced chip manufacturing. The investment aims to create tens of thousands of high-paying jobs and strengthen the U.S. semiconductor supply chain, driven by the surging demand for artificial intelligence.

item.title: [TSM Bullish (+0.46)] TSM Rides on AI, Advanced Nodes & Capacity Expansion: Worth a Buy?
item.description:
Sentiment: TSM Bullish (+0.46)
Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company (TSM) is poised for continued growth driven by the surging demand for AI infrastructure, rapid adoption of advanced process technologies, and expanding global manufacturing capacity. The company reported strong Q2 2026 revenues and expects continued robust demand, especially with the industry's shift towards agentic AI. TSM's leadership in leading-edge nodes like 3nm and the upcoming 2nm and A16 technologies, coupled with international capacity expansions, are strengthening its competitive position and addressable market opportunities.

item.title: [TSM Bullish (+0.48)] TSMC Stock And 2 Global Blue Chips For AI Infrastructure Growth
item.description:
Sentiment: TSM Bullish (+0.48)
This article identifies three multinational blue-chip stocks, Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing (TSMC), Atlas Copco, and Airbus, that are well-positioned for growth amid evolving global trade rules and regulation. It highlights their global reach and role in key sectors like AI infrastructure, industrial capital spending, and aerospace. The article emphasizes how these companies' strategic responses to geopolitical and economic shifts make them compelling investment opportunities.

item.title: [TSM Bearish (-0.35)] Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Co Ltd Stock (TSM) Moved Down by 3.11% on Aug 24: Facts Behind the Movement
item.description:
Sentiment: TSM Bearish (-0.35)
Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Co Ltd (TSM) stock declined by 3.11% on August 24, primarily due to investor profit-taking after a significant rally in the semiconductor sector, exacerbated by concerns over heavy capital expenditures and valuation. Technical indicators show a MACD sell signal and an oversold Williams %R, while fundamental analysis highlights substantial revenue and net profit figures within the Technology Equipment industry. Key risks include surging capital expenditure, valuation premia, geopolitical concentration, and operational complexities from international expansion.

item.title: [TSM Bullish (+0.48)] Unbreakable Shield: Why Taiwan’s Chip Expertise Cannot Be Cloned
item.description:
Sentiment: TSM Bullish (+0.48)
Taiwan's semiconductor industry is a complex ecosystem, far beyond just wafer foundries, encompassing advanced packaging, materials, and a dense network of suppliers and talent. While Taiwan is building new semiconductor plants in the US, Japan, and Europe, this diversification alone will not eliminate global reliance on the island. The article argues that instead of trying to replace Taiwan, the US and Europe should focus on reinforcing Taiwan's resilience and role as a core pillar of the democratic semiconductor alliance by supporting its advancements and aligning industrial policies.

item.description:

This article discusses whether the booming revenue of Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing (TSM) outweighs its geopolitical risks, especially with the proliferation of agentic AI driving further growth.
